gemini.rationale: The transaction is a standard bank merger where Athens and its bank subsidiary merge into CapStar and its bank subsidiary (T3 N-1). The products (T4), processes (T5), and organization (T6) of Athens are absorbed into CapStar, with no documented structural mismatch at closing where products transferred without processes or processes without people.

grok.rationale: gap_45 is 0 because the closing structure is a parallel holding-company and bank-level merger in which Athens Federal’s customer-facing branch/consumer-business products and CapStar’s commercial/private-banking products both move into the single surviving CapStar Bank charter together with the banks’ operations; no product-without-process mismatch is documented at closing (Athens’s data-processing was already third-party outsourced pre-closing). gap_56 is 0 because the same bank-level merger that collapses operations also contractually bridges Athens management/governance via two Athens board seats on CapStar/CapStar Bank and new executive employment agreements effective at closing, so process and organization are structurally aligned rather than severed.

openai.rationale: Athens’s consumer and business banking products and branch-delivery franchise were combined with CapStar’s commercial, private-banking, and correspondent-banking franchise in the surviving bank; although Athens outsourced significant data processing, the slice documents no closing-time product-versus-process mismatch. The management and governance substrate was bridged through two Athens director appointments and new CapStar employment agreements for certain Athens executives, so no incoherent process-versus-organization gap is documented at closing.
